note: Teacher-written reference questions for the sample chapter, used for reference-based evaluation (BLEU / ROUGE-L / concept coverage).

questions.question: What is the process by which green plants convert light energy into chemical energy called?
Why are green plants called autotrophs?
questions.answer: they make their own food from simple inorganic substances

questions.question: What are the raw materials of photosynthesis?
Which gas is released as a by-product of photosynthesis?
What is the main site of photosynthesis in most plants?
In which organelles does photosynthesis take place?
Which green pigment absorbs light energy?
Why do leaves look green?
What is the fluid-filled space of the chloroplast that surrounds the thylakoids called?
Through which pores does gas exchange take place in a leaf?
Which cells control the opening and closing of a stoma?
Where do the light-dependent reactions take place?
What is photolysis?
questions.answer: the splitting of water molecules by light energy

questions.question: Which energy carriers are produced during the light-dependent reactions?
What is the main energy currency of the cell?
Where does the Calvin cycle take place?
What is the first stage of the Calvin cycle?
Which enzyme catalyses carbon fixation?
What is a limiting factor?
questions.answer: a factor that is in shortest supply and therefore restricts the rate of a process

questions.question: Name the main limiting factors of photosynthesis.
questions.answer: light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature

questions.question: What is the compensation point?
questions.answer: the light intensity at which the rate of photosynthesis equals the rate of respiration

questions.question: Why does the rate of photosynthesis fall at very high temperatures?
Which mineral is an essential part of the chlorophyll molecule?
What is chlorosis?
questions.answer: the yellowing of leaves between the veins

questions.question: Which tissue transports water and mineral ions from the roots to the leaves?
What is translocation?
questions.answer: the movement of sucrose and amino acids through the phloem
